correctness.rationale: The k(x,y)=1+x dot y feature map makes simplex quadrature error the origin-to-hull distance because antipodal symmetry centers the sample law. A single angular gap above pi is equivalent to nonzero distance, whose magnitude is sin((G-pi)/2). Complementary-arc integration proves the exact tail and exact anchor law. Positive minimum density gives uniform exponential domination, validating all p>0 moment limits. Strict Jensen gives the moment-order sampling extremum. A standard-library script passed 578 finite diagnostics; infinite quantifiers are proved analytically.

value.rationale: The exact first-harmonic kernel is a canonical finite-rank quadrature testbed; nonnegative optimized weights are central in stable integration. Rare nonrepresentability is exponentially unlikely but its conditional magnitude controls high-order loss. The exact mixture law, all-p coefficients, universal leading mean, and strict optimality reversal of uniform sampling are useful and not a mere bound on a contrived quantity. Does not overclaim general RKHS implications.
